purpose: Prove which Universal Run Kernel surfaces exist in the designated UR-DEV head before G2 acceptance, so no downstream DWO v2 package targets an unimplemented surface.
method: git tree-diff and per-ref blob digest comparison against an exact local gwc checkout; read-only, no mutation.

refs_compared.relation: compare 5c4e4a53...414002f9 reports gwc/main is 6 commits ahead of the UR-DEV head; the merge base is the UR-DEV head, therefore the UR-DEV head is an ancestor of gwc/main.

whole_tree_delta.note: The kernel surface is identical, but the two refs differ elsewhere (tests/test_m1_instruction_convergence.py removed, tests/test_q0_live_qualification_contract.py added). Those differences are outside the kernel contract and do not affect DWO v2 projection semantics.

contract_document_findings.interpretation: The Universal Run Kernel Contract Freeze v1.1 is published as a Notion design artifact, not as a versioned core contract document in the repository. The authoritative machine-readable kernel identity available in-repository is therefore the executable module set plus the SCRUM-668 modules manifest, together with the JCS+SHA-256 content_digest envelope defined by the contract. DWO v2 must treat the Notion contract freeze as the normative specification and the repository modules as its executable realization, and must NOT assume a repository contract document exists to parse.

conclusions.statement: The designated UR-DEV head 5c4e4a53 contains the full Universal Run Kernel executable surface (12 kernel test modules, 24 universal_run paths, SCRUM-668 modules manifest) and that surface is byte-identical to gwc/main.
conclusions.consequence: DWO v2 may bind the designated UR-DEV head as the native semantic source and target the kernel contract. No unimplemented-surface risk from this direction.

conclusions.statement: The Notion-reported tension that the designated head defers executable runtime seams while implementation lives on gwc/main is NOT reproduced by the repository tree. Both refs carry an identical, complete kernel surface.
conclusions.consequence: The tension is a documentation-status conflict, not a code-state conflict. It does not block G2 and must not be treated as BLOCKING_CONTRACT_DRIFT.
conclusions.residual_risk: Documentation status remains contradictory: the Run Model page shows both WAITING_FOR_HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE and IMPLEMENTED/ACCEPTED. Recorded as Q-002, non-blocking for this package.

conclusions.statement: The R1 to R2 binding correction is ADAPTER_CHANGE, confirmed by evidence. The kernel contract is unchanged between the wrong and correct UR-DEV refs, so no reducer, projection, qualification or UI change is implied by the correction itself.
conclusions.consequence: Drift classification ADAPTER_CHANGE stands, verified rather than asserted.

conclusions.statement: The Universal Run Kernel Contract is not materialized as a versioned repository document at any ref.
conclusions.consequence: DWO v2 must not attempt to parse a repository contract document for kernel identity; it must use the Notion contract freeze plus the executable module manifest identity.

grants_no_authority: This artifact is read-only evidence. It grants no G2, G4, merge, deploy, production, data, secret or migration authority.
